sources.title: German Archaeological Institute, Marib: the capital of Saba
sources.note: Original DAI full indexed text read: Overview,98.5 hectares, city gates/zones, earliest layers around1900 BCE, city by early first millennium BCE, likely occupation continuity. Earlier settlement does not prove a kingdom existed in1900 or1500 BCE.

sources.title: German Archaeological Institute, Building investigations of the city walls of Marib and Sirwah
sources.note: Original DAI indexed Results read. Wall height changes could respond to rapid oasis sediment accumulation rather than necessarily military crises; seven identified gates.

sources.title: German Archaeological Institute, The dam of Marib (2019)
sources.note: Original DAI full indexed text read; direct page fetch failed. Reproducible query site:dainst.blog/190JahreDAI/tag-140-der-staudamm-von-marib/ Wasser. Raised/calmed floodwater channelled onto fields, agricultural support for residents/caravans, nearly10000 hectares. Avoid compressing all dam phases into single construction date/dimensions or adopting simplistic Quran/fall narrative.

sources.title: German Archaeological Institute, The Sabaean city of Sirwah: results
sources.note: Direct Results page read. Five-Pillar Building dated around900 BCE by radiocarbon; banquet areas and estimated360 places; chronological concentrations8th-5th BCE and first2centuriesCE; loss of Saba independence late3rdcenturyCE. Banqueting area capacity is reconstructed, not guest-list count.

sources.title: Scuola Normale Superiore, Mnamon: Ancient South Arabian examples of writing
sources.note: Direct scholarly guide and transcriptions/translations read. AO31929 line1 late8thcenturyBCE; RES3913 canal inscription4th-3rdcenturyBCE; Oost.Inst.37 alphabet11th-late6thcenturyBCE; YM11743 Sabaic contract5th-2ndcenturyBCE. Nashshan/as-Sawda finds document Sabaean involvement and regional scribal practice, not uninterrupted sovereignty over that city.

sources.title: Unicode Consortium, Old South Arabian character chart
sources.note: Direct official code chart PDF read, third page. Used only to verify modern digital typesetting of attested mkrb S1bʾ:10A63 m,10A6B k,10A67 r,10A68 b;10A6A s1,10A68 b,10A71 alef. Not an independent historical translation or facsimile of original letter shapes.

sources.title: Louvre, Sabaean inscribed statue base AO4973 / CIH544
sources.note: Direct museum entry and full ten-line French translation read. Sirwah provenance inferred from text, not secure excavation. Numeric date0-300 conflicts with period label first centuryBCE-secondCE; draft gives broad turn-of-era/early-centuries context and no artificial point year. Bronze statues missing; sockets survive.

sources.title: Friedrich Schiller University Jena, Schwerwiegender Bericht eines Königs (2016)
sources.note: Direct university-authored press release hosted by idw read; Norbert Nebes research, Yithaamar inscription,2005 discovery, campaigns and acquisition of land/populations, Queen of Sheba absent from inscriptions. Original edition/reference named. Exact Assyrian synchronisms not treated as universally uncontroversial.

sources.title: Burkhard Vogt, Research on the Great Dam after the2005/2006 season, ZAAK2 (2007),121-141
sources.note: Direct original research abstract read. Journal volume is2007; online posting2023 is not research date. Northern sluice present construction under Abraha548CE; earlier structure probably Sharahbil Yafur456CE and preceding channel. Public wording preserves attribution uncertainty.

batchIdentityNotes.scope: Sabaean kingdom centred Marib/Sirwah in Yemen, distinct from neighbouring Minaean, Qatabanian, Hadrami and Himyarite polities. Regional Sabaic writing at Nashshan/as-Sawda does not imply permanent Sabaean rule there.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Eight imported Polygon snapshots from1500BCE through1BCE; broad southwestern Arabia bounds41.629016E to45.434254E,14.606682N to18.660098N, later western edge42.205022E. Snapshot gap400-323BCE retained, no new geometry.
batchIdentityNotes.dates: Imported -1500,-1 preserved with map_coverage. Earlier Marib settlement around1900BCE is not a founding date. Main documented royal phases first millenniumBCE to late3rdcenturyCE. Periods and later life/repair paragraphs explicitly extend beyond map cutoff.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: AO31929 line1 mkrb S1bʾ, late8thcenturyBCE. Modern Unicode typesetting, not invented text or facsimile. Technical character mapping verified independently in official Unicode chart. Mukarrib not mistranslated as a precisely known modern office.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No new medical treatment, toilet system or universal schooling asserted. Family prayer represents elite dedicants; monumental Five-Pillar Building is not ordinary housing. Louvre family-base date broad due inconsistent catalogue date fields. Dam rebuilding centuries later distinct from Sabaean sovereignty.
